title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, grilled without sauce, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken legs, drumsticks and thighs are dark meat cuts rich in protein and essential micronutrients. Grilled without sauce and with the skin removed, they retain their natural flavor while reducing fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark chicken meat contains more iron and zinc than white meat.
Grilling creates a distinctive aroma through Maillard reactions.
These cuts are staples in many world cuisines, from barbecue to Asian marinades.
Skipping the skin cuts the calorie count by roughly 30%.
Proper grilling keeps the meat juicy and tender.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Dark meat supplies iron, which supports hemoglobin formation and energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc aids immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Chicken legs and thighs contain virtually no carbs, making them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The meat provides vitamin B6 and niacin, important for metabolic processes.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the meat was previously marinated, sodium levels can be high; plain grilling is preferable.

items.title: Undercooking risk
items.content: Chicken must reach an internal temperature of at least 74 °C to eliminate food‑borne pathogens.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage can lead to salmonella growth; keep refrigerated no more than 2 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the portion as a main dish, add to salads, wraps, or use as a sandwich filling. Remove the skin before eating to lower fat intake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked meat in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.
